prompt_hash_contract.downstream_authority: the frozen literal artifact and the preflight manifest, never the pending sentinel
prompt_hash_contract.config_contract_normalization_reason: the CPU preflight materializes these four values, so the field necessarily differs before and after the freeze; normalizing it keeps the post-freeze config amendment contract-neutral for the manifest, genesis ledger and resource ticket pinned at freeze time
prompt_hash_contract.maps_expected_hashes_is_inside_the_contr: maps.expected_hashes is NOT normalized and must remain the literal string PENDING_CPU_PREFLIGHT_AND_FRESH_PAYLOAD_REVIEW for the entire lifecycle; amending it would move the config contract and simultaneously invalidate the pinned code/resource authorization manifest, genesis GPU ledger and resource ticket inside a no-clobber namespace. Materialized map hashes are recorded in the preflight manifest and bound by the payload-hash review manifest, never written back into this field.
prompt_hash_contract.v5_defect_closed: v5 asserted config<->computed prompt-hash equality before the freeze that produces those hashes, so its CPU preflight could never pass its own static gate (job 13805, FAILED 1:0)

v7_scope.changes: the three v6 payload-review Importants, plus one Critical defect discovered while closing I-1
v7_scope.no_scientific_semantic_changed: selection rule, tag, suffix, count, prompt TEXT and its four SHA-256 values, prompt-hash rule, frame rule, transcript rule, reliability thresholds and taxonomy, fallback semantics, role/JL map construction, resource caps and every authorization flag are unchanged in meaning; the v7 tree differs from v6 only by the version-token rename and the four repairs below. The v7 selection was recomputed from the frozen rule and reproduces the v6 allowlists exactly on both datasets.
v7_scope.C1_prompt_render_defect: CRITICAL, found while closing I-1 and repaired here. v6 rendered prompts with PROMPTS[form].format(transcript=...) at producer.py:768, its only call site. Both templates embed _SCHEMA_TEXT, whose literal JSON braces are read by str.format as replacement fields, so every render raises KeyError: '"source_relation"'. No v6 self-test rendered a prompt, so all 25 v6 checks passed. Had v6 been submitted, the job would have loaded the 7B teacher onto the A100 and then died on the FIRST forward, after consuming the single-use resource ticket and entering the no-clobber namespace. v7 replaces the formatter with render_prompt(), a literal single-placeholder substitution; no prompt byte changes and the four frozen prompt hashes are re-asserted by fixture.
v7_scope.I1_teacher_visible_containment: no identifier and no label-bearing substring may reach any teacher-visible field. Enforced as a fail-closed precondition over all 400 identifiers and both prompt forms BEFORE the model is loaded, and re-enforced per item immediately before every forward. HateMM identifiers (hate_video_*, non_hate_video_*) ARE the label, so the sealed ID-only allowlist provides label containment for MHC-ZH only; selection label-blindness is established by hash reproduction, teacher label-blindness by this runtime check.
v7_scope.I2_selection_known_answer: the tautological selection_deterministic self-test is replaced by a pinned known-answer digest vector plus a dataset/identifier sensitivity check
v7_scope.I3_ceilings_are_machine_checked: the 2 GPU-hour tranche ceiling is an in-job absolute deadline computed once at job start, anchored to the allocation entry marker's /proc/uptime reading (not to SLURM_JOB_START_TIME, whose absence would anchor the guard AFTER the wrapper timeout and leave it unable to fire) and held guard_item_margin_seconds ahead of the wrapper timeout so it stops cleanly before an item instead of the wrapper killing a forward mid-flight; it may only STOP work before an item begins, never truncate or alter an output, and a breach writes an accounting-only record and exits 40. The campaign ceiling is checked at job start against artifacts/c04/campaign/gpu_ledger.json before the single-use ticket is consumed, and written back from sacct by a campaign-record stage that does NOT depend on the seal, so a breach, watchdog TERM, OOM or HALT is accounted for too. The EFFECTIVE ceiling is min(phase cap, aggregate cap): the amendment binds the approved first tranche at 2 GPU-hours across all C04 jobs, and only the conditional full-bank tranche raises it to 8.
v7_scope.v7_round_2_repairs: Round-1 independent review returned REVISE 2C/2H/3I, all confirmed and repaired: C-A the reconciler's strict provisional-usage key set was not updated alongside the writer, which would have halted the terminal reconciliation of a fully paid-for tranche inside a no-clobber namespace (now a single shared key-set constant, a shared builder and a fixture); C-B proposition_cosine could exceed the schema's maximum:1 by one ulp whenever the two forms agreed exactly, failing validation after all 800 forwards (now clamped to its own mathematical range, which changes no comparison outcome against the 0.80 floor); H-A the campaign write side was reachable only on the sealed path; H-B the guard had no enforced margin over the wrapper timeout and could not fire at all without SLURM_JOB_START_TIME; I-C1 the phase cap; I-C2 subsumed by the H-B margin; I-C3 the CPU preflight never round-tripped a record against a downstream contract, which is the blind spot that let both Criticals through and is the same shape as v6 never rendering a prompt in a self-test.
v7_scope.v7_round_3_repairs: Round-2 independent review returned REVISE 0C/2H/3I (both round-1 Criticals confirmed closed). All five repaired: H-1 the campaign accumulator could brick itself -- an over-cap row was written and THEN raised, after which every later load raised forever, destroying the one artifact meant to outlive every namespace (loading is now accounting and never refuses; refusal moved wholly to the authorization side, every rejecting check runs before the write, and an over-ceiling total is recorded with a flag that refuses the NEXT allocation); H-2 the reader's key set was still a hand-written twin of the writer's and the fixture self-compared, so one-sided drift stayed invisible (the reader now imports and uses the shared constants, making drift impossible by construction); I-1 cosine lived in producer.py, which the CPU preflight never imports, so deleting the C-B clamp left every fixture green (cosine moved into the contract module and covered by fixtures); I-2 the post-loop canonicalization and seal phase was unguarded and had to fit inside a margin sized for one item (a new guard_seal_reserve_seconds is required before that phase begins, so an overrun stops cleanly with a breach record instead of being SIGTERM'd mid-write into an unresumable tranche); I-3 GPU-seconds burned by an allocation that HALTed before claim() published were recorded nowhere (campaign-record now falls back to the allocation entry marker, which the wrapper writes before its first Python call and which therefore exists on every path where the allocation was entered).
v7_scope.v7_round_4_repairs: Round-3 independent review returned REVISE 0C/1H/3I and confirmed every round-1 and round-2 finding closed. All four repaired: H-1 the GPU wrapper created the no-clobber namespace and wrote the allocation entry marker BEFORE any code read an authorization flag, so a submission made in the repository's normal gpu_authorized:false state would have made the CPU preflight refuse that namespace forever and forced a v8 rebuild -- the wrapper now carries the sibling wrappers' jq authorization gate plus a frozen-preflight-manifest existence test ahead of the mkdir; I-1 the watchdog reserve rose from 120s to 300s and an over-cap terminal elapsed is now recorded and flagged rather than refused, so a marginal over-run can no longer make the terminal resource state permanently unpublishable; I-2 reconcile-terminal was seal-dependent, so exactly the clean-breach path the budget guard exists to create left the namespace ledger holding a 7200s reservation forever -- the lineage check now has a seal-free tail and a final state is published on every terminal path with seal_published:false; I-3 the three remaining duplicated writer/reader key-set contracts (GPU ledger, allocation claim, resource ticket) are shared constants asserted on both sides, and full prompt_record and canonical_record round-trip fixtures were added across all four reliability regimes plus the zero-frame case, with a non-vacuity check.
v7_scope.v7_round_5_repair: Round-4 independent review returned REVISE 0C/1H/0I and confirmed every round-1, round-2 and round-3 finding closed except one it relocated. The single High: round 4 widened resource_final_state.schema.json to accept the NO_SEAL_PUBLISHED sentinel but not stage_authorization.schema.json, whose reconciliation payload_binding still pinned provisional_gpu_usage_sha256 to 64-hex -- so on every non-sealing terminal path the code required an authorization manifest carrying a sentinel its own frozen schema forbade, the intersection was empty, and resource_final_state.json could never be published on exactly the paths the seal-free tail exists to serve. Closed by mirroring the anyOf into the stage-authorization schema, plus two fixtures that round-trip a full reconciliation manifest through validate_schema in BOTH seal regimes and confirm a foreign pin is still refused.
